formats.name: cbor
formats.description: Bulk import and export of CBOR row files (CBOR Sequence (RFC 8742)), one item per row
formats.comment: Load a CBOR row file (CBOR Sequence (RFC 8742)) into the COPY target table

tags.vgi.doc_llm:
Bulk-move whole tables in and out of CBOR data files — the row-file counterpart to the per-blob `decode` scalar. The file is a CBOR Sequence (RFC 8742): one top-level item per row, with no container header or footer, so it appends and streams. The same format name serves both directions, and a file written by one round-trips through the other. The `FORMAT` identifier is scoped by the ATTACH alias, so it reads `<alias>.cbor`:

```sql
COPY (<query>) TO '<path>' (FORMAT '<alias>.cbor');
COPY <table> FROM '<path>' (FORMAT '<alias>.cbor');
```

With the default `row_format 'map'` each item is a map keyed by column name: self-describing, so on read the columns may appear in any order, a key absent from an item reads as NULL, and extra keys are ignored. `row_format 'array'` frames each row as an array of values in column order — more compact, but positional. Column values encode exactly as the `encode` scalar does (shortest-lossless integers and floats, `BLOB` as a byte string, `TIMESTAMP` as an epoch instant, `LIST` / `STRUCT` / `MAP` as arrays and maps) and decode back onto the COPY target's exact column types. A value that cannot be represented in its target column fails the COPY with a column-qualified message; `ignore_errors true` instead skips unusable rows and tolerates a truncated trailing item. Rows are written in source order, so an ordered source query keeps its ordering in the file. On write, `canonical 'core'` (RFC 8949 §4.2.1) or `canonical 'ctap2'` orders map keys deterministically, so the same rows always produce byte-identical output.

**Paths resolve on the worker.** The file is opened by the worker process, so the path is interpreted against its filesystem and working directory — not the SQL client's. That is invisible when DuckDB spawns the worker locally, but a worker in a container or on another host cannot see the caller's paths: use a location both sides agree on (a mounted volume), and prefer absolute paths. A path the worker cannot open is reported with the directory it actually looked in.

tags.vgi.result_dynamic_columns_md:
### Read direction — columns mirror the COPY target

The scan emits exactly the COPY target table's columns, in its declared order and types: DuckDB fixes them from the target and the reader projects each CBOR item onto them, inserting no cast. There is no independent result schema, so the shape below is one worked variant — a target declared `(id INTEGER, name VARCHAR, seen TIMESTAMP)`.

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| id | INTEGER | The item's value for the `id` column — by key name under `row_format 'map'`, by position under `row_format 'array'`. |
| name | VARCHAR | The item's value for the `name` column. A nested value lands as its JSON text. |
| seen | TIMESTAMP | The item's value for the `seen` column, read from an epoch instant. A key absent from the item reads as `NULL`. |
tags.vgi.title: CBOR Row Files (COPY FROM / TO)

options.name: row_format
options.description: How each row is framed as one item: 'map' (default) keys it by column name; 'array' writes the values positionally in column order.

options.name: ignore_errors
options.description: Skip rows that cannot be projected onto the target columns, and accept a truncated trailing item, instead of failing the COPY (default false).

options.name: canonical
options.description: Deterministic map-key ordering to apply: 'core' (RFC 8949 §4.2.1) or 'ctap2'. Unset keeps ciborium's shortest-form output with keys in column order.

formats.name: fixed
formats.description: Read a fixed-width / flat-file / COBOL-copybook file into the COPY target table (the COPY-FROM counterpart of read_fixed)
formats.comment: Load a fixed-width / flat-file / COBOL-copybook file into the COPY target table

tags.vgi.doc_llm:
Load a fixed-width / flat-file / COBOL-copybook file straight into a DuckDB table — the COPY-FROM counterpart of read_fixed. It is invoked as a COPY statement (not called directly):

```sql
COPY <table> FROM '<path>' (FORMAT 'fixed.fixed', spec '<layout>');
```

The format name is catalog-qualified by the ATTACH name (e.g. 'fixed.fixed'). Each record is decoded per the `spec` option (a Perl/Python `unpack` template, a JSON field list, or a COBOL copybook; auto-detected unless `format` is given) and the decoded columns are assigned to the COPY target table's columns BY POSITION and cast to each target column's type, so the spec must produce the same number of columns in the same order. Options are named: `spec` (required), `format`, `encoding` ('ascii'/'ebcdic'), `framing` ('newline'/'fixed'/'rdw'/'rdw_blocked'), `record_length` (bytes, 'fixed' framing only), plus `endpoint`/`region`/`url_style`/`use_ssl` for `s3://` sources. `path` may be local, `s3://`, or `http(s)://`. Use it to ingest mainframe or legacy flat-file data into an existing table without a read_fixed call.
tags.vgi.doc_md:
Load a fixed-width file into a table:

```sql
COPY <table> FROM '<path>' (FORMAT 'fixed.fixed', spec '<layout>');
```

Decoded columns map to the target table's columns by position (cast to each type). Named options: `spec` (required), `format`, `encoding`, `framing`, `record_length`, and S3 overrides. The COPY-FROM counterpart of `read_fixed`.
tags.vgi.result_dynamic_columns_md:
`copy_fixed` is invoked through `COPY <table> FROM '<path>' (FORMAT 'fixed.fixed', …)`, not as a table function, so it returns **no result set of its own**. The rows decoded from the file are inserted into the COPY **target table**, and DuckDB reports the number of rows loaded as the statement's `Count`. The materialized columns are therefore the target table's own columns — each decoded field is mapped to a target column **by position** and cast to that column's type, so the `spec` must produce the same number of columns, in the same order, as the table.

For a target table `accounts(name VARCHAR, qty INTEGER)` loaded with the spec `name:A10 qty:9(5)`, the loaded columns are:

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | VARCHAR | The target column populated from the first decoded field (bytes 0–9). |
| `qty` | INTEGER | The target column populated from the second decoded field, cast from the 5-digit value. |
tags.vgi.title: Load Fixed-Width File (COPY FROM)

options.name: spec
options.description: The record layout to decode each row with: a Perl/Python `unpack` template, a JSON field list, or a COBOL copybook. The decoded columns are assigned to the COPY target table's columns by position, so the spec must produce the same number of columns in the same order (each cast to the target column's type).

options.name: format
options.description: Force how `spec` is interpreted: 'template', 'json', or 'copybook'. Omit to auto-detect.

options.name: encoding
options.description: Byte encoding of the file: 'ascii' (the default) or 'ebcdic' (CP037).

options.name: framing
options.description: How records are delimited: 'newline' (the default), 'fixed', 'rdw', or 'rdw_blocked'.

options.name: record_length
options.description: The length of each record in BYTES; used only for 'fixed' framing. Defaults to the length implied by the layout `spec`.

options.name: compression
options.description: Input compression: 'auto' (the default — detect gzip/zstd from the file's magic bytes, else read raw), 'none', 'gzip', or 'zstd'. Applies to local and cloud paths alike; decompression happens before framing/decoding.

options.name: max_decompressed_bytes
options.description: Safety cap on total DECOMPRESSED bytes per file (a decompression-bomb backstop; default 16 GiB). Only applies to gzip/zstd input. Raise it to load a legitimately huge compressed file.

options.name: endpoint
options.description: Custom S3 endpoint for an `s3://` source (e.g. MinIO/R2 'host:9000'); overrides any endpoint from a CREATE SECRET.

options.name: region
options.description: AWS region for an `s3://` source. Overrides the region from a CREATE SECRET.

options.name: url_style
options.description: S3 addressing for an `s3://` source: 'path' (path-style, e.g. MinIO) or 'vhost'.

options.name: use_ssl
options.description: Whether to use TLS for an `s3://` source's custom endpoint (default true).

formats.name: fixed_out
formats.description: Write the COPY source out to a fixed-width / flat-file / COBOL-copybook file (the COPY-TO counterpart of write_fixed)
formats.comment: Write the COPY source out to a fixed-width / flat-file / COBOL-copybook file

tags.vgi.doc_llm:
Write a query or table out to a fixed-width / flat-file / COBOL-copybook file — the COPY-TO counterpart of write_fixed. It is invoked as a COPY statement (not called directly):

```sql
COPY (<query>|<table>) TO '<path>' (FORMAT 'fixed.fixed_out', spec '<layout>');
```

The writer uses a DISTINCT format name 'fixed.fixed_out' (catalog-qualified by the ATTACH name) because the VGI SDK advertises FROM and TO as separate formats. Each input column is matched to a layout field BY NAME, encoded to record bytes per the `spec` option (a Perl/Python `unpack` template, a JSON field list, or a COBOL copybook; auto-detected unless `format` is given), framed per `framing`, and written to `<path>` (overwritten if it exists). Options are named: `spec` (required), `format`, `encoding` ('ascii'/'ebcdic'), `framing` ('newline'/'fixed'/'rdw'/'rdw_blocked'), plus `endpoint`/`region`/`url_style`/`use_ssl` for `s3://` destinations. NOTE: CREATE SECRET credentials are NOT forwarded on the COPY-TO path — use named S3 overrides, ambient credentials, or write_fixed for secret-backed cloud writes.
tags.vgi.doc_md:
Write a relation to a fixed-width file:

```sql
COPY (<query>|<table>) TO '<path>' (FORMAT 'fixed.fixed_out', spec '<layout>');
```

Input columns map to layout fields by name. Named options: `spec` (required), `format`, `encoding`, `framing`, and S3 overrides. The COPY-TO counterpart of `write_fixed`.
tags.vgi.result_dynamic_columns_md:
`copy_to_fixed` is invoked through `COPY (<query>|<table>) TO '<path>' (FORMAT 'fixed.fixed_out', …)`, not as a table function, so it returns **no result set of its own**. The COPY source rows are encoded to fixed-width records and written to `<path>` (overwritten if it exists); each input column is matched to a layout field **by name** before encoding. DuckDB reports only a single value — the number of rows written:

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Count` | BIGINT | The number of source rows written to the file, reported by DuckDB as the `COPY … TO` statement's result. |
tags.vgi.title: Write Fixed-Width File (COPY TO)

formats.name: pmtiles
formats.description: COPY ... TO format that encodes rows with a GEOMETRY column as a PMTiles vector tileset
formats.comment: Vector tiles (MVT) in a PMTiles v3 archive

tags.vgi.doc_llm: A COPY TO format, not a table function: use it as FORMAT 'mvt.pmtiles' in a COPY ... TO statement whose destination is a local .pmtiles path. Each row is a feature. The `GEOMETRY` column must be WGS84 lon/lat (or EPSG:3857). A `VARCHAR` column named `layer` (or `layer_column`) names each row's layer, so one COPY can write several layers via UNION ALL; without it every row goes to `layer` (default: the file name). A column named `feature_id` (or `id_column`) becomes the feature id, and a column named `properties` holding JSON objects is expanded into attributes, so read_tiles output can be written back. Every other column becomes an attribute (`VARCHAR`, numbers, `BOOLEAN`; dates as ISO text; lists and structs as JSON text); NULLs are omitted. Options: minzoom/maxzoom (default 0/14); minzoom_column/maxzoom_column for per-feature zoom ranges; simplify and buffer (pixels of a 256-pixel tile); extent (4096); max_tile_bytes (500000: fails rather than dropping features); max_tiles; name, description, attribution. ORDER BY sets drawing order. COPY reports the number of rows written.
tags.vgi.doc_md:
## COPY ... TO (FORMAT 'mvt.pmtiles')

Encode a query's rows as Mapbox Vector Tiles in a PMTiles archive. One row is one feature; a `layer` column puts rows in different layers of the same tiles, so a single COPY of a `UNION ALL` writes a whole multi-layer basemap.
tags.vgi.example_queries: [{"description": "Write two cities as a one-layer tileset (zoom 0 to 8)", "sql": "COPY (SELECT 'cities' AS layer, name, population, ST_Point(lon, lat) AS geometry FROM (VALUES ('Rome', 2800000, 12.5, 41.9), ('Paris', 2100000, 2.35, 48.86)) t(name, population, lon, lat)) TO 'cities.pmtiles' (FORMAT 'mvt.pmtiles', maxzoom 8)"}, {"description": "Re-tile every layer of an existing tileset into a new archive", "sql": "COPY (SELECT layer, feature_id, properties, geometry FROM mvt.main.read_tiles('test/fixtures/sample.pmtiles')) TO 'sample-copy.pmtiles' (FORMAT 'mvt.pmtiles', maxzoom 4, name 'sample copy')"}]
tags.vgi.title: Write PMTiles

options.name: attribution
options.description: Attribution (HTML) in the metadata

options.name: buffer
options.description: Margin around each tile, in pixels of a 256-pixel tile

options.name: description
options.description: Tileset description in the metadata

options.name: extent
options.description: Tile coordinate grid size (units per tile edge)

options.name: geometry_column
options.description: GEOMETRY column to encode (default: the only GEOMETRY column)

options.name: id_column
options.description: Column of non-negative feature ids (default: a column named feature_id)

options.name: layer
options.description: Layer name for rows without a layer column (default: the file name without .pmtiles)

options.name: layer_column
options.description: Column holding each row's layer name (default: a column named layer)

options.name: max_tile_bytes
options.description: Fail if a compressed tile is larger than this (0: no limit)

options.name: max_tiles
options.description: Fail if the tileset would have more tiles than this

options.name: maxzoom
options.description: Highest zoom level to write

options.name: maxzoom_column
options.description: Column giving the highest zoom each feature appears at

options.name: minzoom
options.description: Lowest zoom level to write

options.name: minzoom_column
options.description: Column giving the lowest zoom each feature appears at

options.name: name
options.description: Tileset name in the metadata (default: the file name)

options.name: properties_column
options.description: Column of JSON objects whose keys become attributes (default: a column named properties)

options.name: simplify
options.description: Line and polygon simplification tolerance, in pixels of a 256-pixel tile (0 turns it off)
